properties.name: Kellum-Noble House (Sam Houston Park)
properties.designation_full: City of Houston Protected Landmark & Recorded Texas Historic Landmark
properties.description: The oldest surviving building in Houston on its original brick foundation. Built during the Texas Republic era by Nathaniel Kellum, later home to Houston's first public school.

properties.name: Church of the Annunciation
properties.description: Houston's oldest continuously operating church parish, constructed with red pressed brick and featuring a soaring 180-foot spire designed by renowned Galveston architect Nicholas Clayton in 1884.

properties.name: 1884 Houston Cotton Exchange
properties.designation_full: City of Houston Protected Landmark & NRHP
properties.description: Grand headquarters of the Texas cotton trade designed by landmark architect Eugene Heiner. Features red pressed brick, ornate Galveston-carved limestone keystones, and grand ballroom trading floors.

properties.name: Sweeney, Coombs & Fredericks Building
properties.description: Notable Queen Anne commercial structure on Main Street crowned with a three-story circular corner turret, decorative cast iron, and sunburst panels, home to landmark jewelry firms.

properties.name: Market Square Historic Public Park
properties.architect: George E. Dickey / City of Houston
properties.description: Houston's original civic center, site of four successive City Halls and market buildings from 1841 to 1960. Today forms the cultural epicenter of historic downtown.

properties.name: The Rice Hotel
properties.description: Historic 17-story Beaux-Arts hotel built by Jesse H. Jones on the former capitol grounds of the Republic of Texas. Site of President John F. Kennedy's final public speech on November 21, 1963.

properties.name: Julia Ideson Building
properties.architect: Ralph Adams Cram & William Ward Watkin
properties.designation_full: City of Houston Protected Landmark & NRHP
properties.description: Houston's monumental central library from 1926 to 1976, renowned for its Spanish Renaissance cloisters, vibrant bas-relief terracotta, and historic WPA-era art and indoor loggias.

properties.name: Niels & Mellie Esperson Buildings
properties.description: Houston's only complete Italian Renaissance skyscraper, commissioned by pioneer businesswoman Mellie Esperson in tribute to Niels Esperson. Crowned with an ornate 38-foot circular tempietto.

properties.name: Gulf Building (JPMorgan Chase)
properties.designation_full: City of Houston Protected Landmark & National Historic Landmark
properties.description: Monumental 36-story Art Deco skyscraper commissioned by Jesse H. Jones for Gulf Oil, standing as Houston's tallest building until 1963. Features 8 grand lobby frescoes depicting Texas history.

properties.name: The Heights Theater
properties.description: Historic cinema that anchored 19th Street social and cultural life for decades. Expertly restored and repurposed as an intimate live performance venue and preservation showpiece.
